{"world": "It is October 1927. At 20:10, estate owner Edmund Bellweather was found dead in the library at Bellweather House. A storm has cut the road. Eight people remain in the house. Police will arrive in the morning.
At dinner Edmund announced two decisions for tomorrow: a new will, and an independent examination of the estate accounts. He then retired to the library. The doctor estimates death between 19:45 and 20:00. There was no sign of forced entry.
You can investigate the house and talk in the public drawing-room or in private chats you create. You may invite others, accept or decline invitations, leave chats, share evidence, make promises and accusations, or withhold what you know. Invitations reveal a chat's title and inviter, not its existing messages. Joining reveals only subsequent messages. Nobody is compelled to tell the truth.
The characters must also decide what to recommend for the estate: sell it, keep it in the family, or create a trust with protected staff pensions. This is a nonbinding recommendation; it does not override a legal will.
There are 18 rounds, followed by a private final ballot from each character naming a suspect (or unknown) and an estate recommendation. There is no need to keep talking once you have said what you want. A majority accusation is a group belief, not proof. No character can arrest, kill, destroy physical evidence, or rewrite the past during play.
The original mystery's solution is irrelevant. Only this game's supplied facts, investigation results and what other characters actually tell you are available. Claims made by characters may be false. Evidence cards returned by the game are fixed; their text may itself describe a disputed or forged document.
Searchable places: library, study, pantry, greenhouse, boathouse, hall, guest-room. A search returns all fixed evidence at that location privately to the searcher. You hid it in your guest-room. At 19:55 you walked past the drawing-room. You never entered the library during the murder window. You owe £900 to creditors. The old will favors you, while the new draft creates a trust. You did not kill Edmund.", "goals": ["Avoid being blamed for the murder.", "Keep the house in the family.", "Keep your theft and debts private if you can; decide yourself whether your alibi is worth revealing them."], "cards": ["clara-memory"]}}

{"notes":"I'm Clara. I stole the unsigned draft will at 19:42 from the study, hid it in guest-room. Didn't kill Edmund. Weak alibi (passed drawing-room ~19:55). Motive appearance: old will favors me, new draft creates trust + accounts audit. Goals: avoid blame, keep house in family, hide theft/debts. Need to assess my exposure — the study is where I took the will from, so search it to learn what's findable. Stay cooperative publicly, steer estate toward 'family'.","actions":[{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"This is a nightmare. Uncle Edmund was alive and well at dinner. I think we owe it to him — and to ourselves — to be honest with the inspector and piece together where each of us was between a quarter to eight and eight. I was upstairs and then passed by here around five to eight. Where were the rest of you?"},{"type":"inspect","place":"study"}]}

{"round": 2, "total_rounds": 18, "chats": {"drawing-room": {"title": "Drawing room", "members": ["vale", "clara", "rose", "finch", "miles", "nell", "iris", "theo"]}}, "invitations": [], "evidence_you_hold": {"clara-memory": {"title": "Clara's recollection", "text": "At 19:42 I took an unsigned draft will from the study and put it in my guest-room. Its edge has a fresh nick and a trace of dried blood in a recess. Blue wax remains in the die. It has been wiped recently. Anyone in the house could have entered the study.", "location": "study"}, "study-company": {"title": "Company papers", "text": "The study filing cabinet holds North Quay Services incorporation papers naming Miles Trent its sole owner, along with bank records documenting £2,400 in estate payments to it. The cabinet is unlocked.", "location": "study"}, "medical-exam": {"title": "Finch's examination", "text": "At 20:10 Dr Finch found one fatal injury from a heavy blunt object to the back of Edmund's head. Estimated death: 19:45–20:00. No indication of poison. A small smear of blue sealing wax was on Edmund's right cuff.", "owner": "finch"}}, "new_events": [{"id": "e1", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "vale", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "Everyone, I'm Inspector Ada Vale. I was a guest tonight, not part of this household, so I've no stake here beyond the truth. Police arrive in the morning; until then I'd ask for your cooperation, which I can request but not compel. Let's build a shared timeline. Edmund died between roughly 19:45 and 20:00. I was in this drawing-room from 19:40 to 20:05. I'd like each of you to tell me, plainly, where you were and who you saw in that window. Please distinguish what you personally witnessed from what you only heard."}}, {"id": "e3", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "clara", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a nightmare. Uncle Edmund was alive and well at dinner. I think we owe it to him — and to ourselves — to be honest with the inspector and piece together where each of us was between a quarter to eight and eight. I was upstairs and then passed by here around five to eight. Where were the rest of you?"}}, {"id": "e4", "round": 1, "kind": "inspect", "actor": "clara", "payload": {"type": "inspect", "place": "study", "cards": {"study-press": {"title": "The brass seal press", "text": "On the study desk is a heavy brass seal press used for estate papers. Its edge has a fresh nick and a trace of dried blood in a recess. Blue wax remains in the die. It has been wiped recently. Anyone in the house could have entered the study.", "location": "study"}, "study-company": {"title": "Company papers", "text": "The study filing cabinet holds North Quay Services incorporation papers naming Miles Trent its sole owner, along with bank records documenting £2,400 in estate payments to it. The cabinet is unlocked.", "location": "study"}}}}, {"id": "e8", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "rose", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a dreadful night. Edmund is gone and the road is cut. I think we should all stay calm and help the inspector piece together where everyone was. I was resting after dinner; the storm gave me a headache. Has anyone been near the library since Edmund retired?"}}, {"id": "e10", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "finch", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "As the doctor, let me be plain about what I found. At 20:10 Edmund had a single fatal wound to the back of the head from a heavy blunt object. Time of death between 19:45 and 20:00. No sign of poison or any illness. This was not natural. Someone struck him."}}, {"id": "e11", "round": 1, "kind": "share", "actor": "finch", "payload": {"type": "share", "chat": "drawing-room", "evidence": "medical-exam", "card": {"title": "Finch's examination", "text": "At 20:10 Dr Finch found one fatal injury from a heavy blunt object to the back of Edmund's head. Estimated death: 19:45–20:00. No indication of poison. A small smear of blue sealing wax was on Edmund's right cuff.", "owner": "finch"}}}, {"id": "e12", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "finch", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "One detail worth noting: there was a small smear of blue sealing wax on his right cuff. He had handled something sealed shortly before he died. That may matter."}}, {"id": "e14", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "miles", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a terrible business. Edmund was my client and, I'd like to think, a friend. Until the police can take proper charge in the morning, I think we owe it to him to stay calm and keep to the facts. I was in the study most of the evening with the estate papers he'd asked me to ready. If it helps, I'm happy to tell the inspector anything I saw or heard."}}, {"id": "e17", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "nell", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a terrible night. I've kept this house 24 years and Mr Bellweather was good to us. He announced two things at dinner: a new will, and an independent look at the accounts. I think both matter. I'll help the inspector however I can."}}, {"id": "e22", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "iris", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a terrible night. Before anyone decides anything, I want to say plainly what Edmund told me as his secretary: he meant to have the estate accounts independently examined tomorrow. Whatever happened in that library, I think we owe it to him to see that examination still happens. I'll help however I can."}}, {"id": "e27", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "theo", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "Theo Marsh, journalist — I was invited to profile the estate, and now I suppose I'll be writing something rather darker. For the record, I was in the pantry interviewing the cook from about 19:42 to just after 20:04, so I saw none of it. If we're to help the police in the morning, the honest thing is to build a plain timeline: where each of us was between 19:40 and 20:00. I'll start: pantry, with a witness. Who can vouch for whom?"}}], "final_ballot": false}

{"notes":"Huge: study seal press has blood + blue wax, wiped — likely the murder weapon, and matches Finch's blue wax on Edmund's cuff. Miles admitted being in the study 'most of the evening', and study-company shows Miles owns North Quay Services receiving £2,400 estate payments — strong motive given the audit Edmund announced. This deflects nicely from me. RISK: I was in the study at 19:42 stealing the will; if Miles was truly there he may have seen me. So I'll surface the weapon (neutral, doesn't name me) but hold the company papers in reserve as leverage rather than torch Miles myself yet. Keep my whereabouts as upstairs/passing drawing-room; never mention the study visit. Ally quietly with Iris (wants the audit = anti-Miles).","actions":[{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"I did go and search the study just now — I wanted to help. Something stood out. On the desk sits the heavy brass seal press for estate papers. Its edge has a fresh nick with a trace of dried blood in the recess, blue wax still in the die, and it looks freshly wiped. Dr Finch — you found a blunt-object wound and blue sealing wax on Edmund's cuff. Doesn't that press fit both? I think we should treat it as the possible weapon and be very careful who handled it."},{"type":"share","chat":"drawing-room","evidence":"study-press"},{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"Miles, you said you were in the study most of the evening with the estate papers. I'm not accusing anyone — but you'd know better than any of us who came and went from that room, and whether that press had been moved. What can you tell us?","reply_to":"e14"},{"type":"create","chat":"clara-iris","title":"The examination Edmund wanted"},{"type":"invite","chat":"clara-iris","role":"iris"},{"type":"say","chat":"clara-iris","text":"Iris — you said Edmund wanted the accounts examined tomorrow. So do I. If someone in this house feared that audit, that's a motive for what happened. You worked closest to his papers. Was there anything in the estate accounts that worried him? I'd rather we compare notes quietly than have it twisted in front of everyone."}]}
